last_assistant_message:
Research complete. Findings:

**Schema verification — unchanged.** `git log --oneline -- sanity/schemas/tool.ts` in `/Users/mdostal/Code/personal-site` shows only one commit, `f25b1e3`, still HEAD for that path — nothing has landed since planning. Full read of `/Users/mdostal/Code/personal-site/sanity/schemas/tool.ts` confirms:
- `hidden`: boolean, `initialValue: false`, description "Same pattern as Case Study's hidden flag: build/review here before it goes live." Matches design-discussion.md §2 exactly.
- `live`: boolean, `initialValue: false`, description confirms it gates both the card's Open-link behavior and rewrite generation — separate gate from `hidden`, as planning assumed.
- Required (`Rule.required()`) fields: `label` (string), `mount` (slug), `description` (text), `originUrl` (url), `repoUrl` (url), `screenshot` (image). Exactly matches the story's assumption. `pagesUrl`, `components`, `sortOrder` remain optional, non-required.
- No schema change needed in personal-site for this story — confirmed correct.

**`scripts/migrate-tools-to-sanity.mjs`** (full read) — the precedent pattern:
- ESM `.mjs`, `createClient` from `@sanity/client`, `apiVersion: "2025-02-19"`, `useCdn: false` (write path).
- Config strictly from `process.env` (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET` default `"production"`, `SANITY_API_WRITE_TOKEN`) — hard exits with an error message if project ID or token missing.
- Idempotency pattern: deterministic `_id` as `` `tool-${mount}` `` + `client.createOrReplace(doc)` — the crawler should reuse this exact `tool-<mount>` id convention to stay collision-safe/re-runnable.
- Screenshot handled via `client.assets.upload("image", buffer, { filename })` then referenced as `{ _type: "image", asset: { _type: "reference", _ref: asset._id } }`.
- `mount` field written as `{ _type: "slug", current: mount }`, not a bare string.
- Optional fields (`pagesUrl`, `components`) conditionally attached only if present, keeping the doc payload minimal otherwise.

**`src/lib/sanity.ts`** — read-only client pattern to mirror for reads:
- `useCdn: true`, `perspective: "published"`, same `apiVersion`. No token (read-only, public dataset).
- `allToolsQuery` GROQ: `*[_type == "tool" && hidden != true] | order(sortOrder asc) { ... }` — useful for the crawler to dedupe against already-listed tools by mount/label.

**Import-alias gotcha — not relevant to the crawler.** `src/lib/tools.ts` has a comment explaining it uses a *relative* `./sanity` import instead of the `@/lib/sanity` alias specifically because `next.config.ts`'s lightweight config-transpile step fails to resolve second-level path aliases (confirmed by a real build failure). This is Next.js build-time-only tooling concern. `scripts/crawl-github-repos.mjs` runs standalone via `node`/`pnpm`, never through Next's config transpiler, so this constraint doesn't apply — it can use whatever import style is simplest (the migrate script uses no aliases at all, just relative/package imports, which is the safer precedent to follow anyway).
